pool.text: General Moses Cleaveland founded the city near the mouth of the Cuyahoga River.
The village of Cleveland was officially incorporated through the efforts of Alfred Kelley.
Cleveland was incorporated as a city while positioned on the eastern river banks.
The neighboring municipality of Ohio City was annexed by the growing city.
The five-story Cleveland Arcade was built and later renovated into a hotel.
Jones Day, one of the largest U.S. law firms, was founded.
The city hosted the first National Air Races and the Women's Air Derby.
The Cleveland Botanical Garden was established in University Circle.
Joe Shuster and Jerry Siegel created the comic book character Superman.
The Great Lakes Exposition debuted at North Coast Harbor to revitalize the city.
The local baseball franchise won another World Series title.
The Hough riots erupted during a tense summer period.
The municipality elected its first African American mayor.
Cleveland became the first city in the nation to have a direct rail transit connection.
A river fire brought national attention to local industrial pollution.
The local government entered a financial default on federal loans.
The annual Tri-C Jazz Fest began at Playhouse Square.
The Great Lakes Burning River Fest began as a music and beer event.
The comedy television series Hot in Cleveland premiered on TV Land.
The Global Center for Health Innovation opened with massive display space.
